    Reference · Python 3.9+ · no build step

    Run from source

    Clone the repo, make a Python 3.9+ virtualenv, run ./run.sh, and open http://127.0.0.1:8420 — with every environment variable, the mock-mode switch, and how the Guide is served at /about/.

    The desktop apps are convenient; the source is the thing itself. Running from a checkout gives you the same server, the same dashboard and the same scheduler, plus the command-line tools the packaged app does not expose. It is also the honest answer to “should I trust an unsigned binary?” — you can read every line first.

    What you need#

    • Python 3.9 or newer. The code is kept 3.9-compatible on purpose (the owner’s Mac runs 3.9.6); the CI builds use 3.11. No match statements, no X | Y unions — if you send a patch, keep it that way.
    • git, and access to the seaneven-web/bablytics repository (private at the time of writing — ask Sean).
    • Roughly a gigabyte of disk for the virtualenv: numpy, pandas, scikit-learn, reportlab and friends.
    • Internet access for market data and news. An Anthropic API key is optional — without one the app runs in mock mode.
    • No Node, no bundler, no database server. The web UI is vanilla JS served straight from web/; the database is a SQLite file.

    Quickstart (macOS / Linux)#

    git clone git@github.com:seaneven-web/bablytics.git Stonks
cd Stonks
python3 -m venv .venv
./.venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt
cp .env.example .env        # optional: add ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
./run.sh                    # or: ./.venv/bin/python -m bablytics.server

    Open http://127.0.0.1:8420. On a fresh checkout there are no users, so the sign-in card offers to create the single local account (username + password, at least 8 characters; the session is a 30-day httponly cookie). Then press Run briefing now on the dashboard to watch a full morning pipeline run without waiting for 7:00 AM.

    The folder is called Stonks out of habit — that was the project’s name through round 4 — and legacy STONKS_* environment variables still work as fallbacks. An old data/stonks.db is renamed to bablytics.db automatically on first start.

    Windows#

    git clone https://github.com/seaneven-web/bablytics.git Stonks
cd Stonks
py -3 -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\pip install -r requirements.txt
copy .env.example .env
.venv\Scripts\python -m bablytics.server

    Configuration — the .env file#

    bablytics/config.py loads .env from the repository root (the packaged app loads it from the data folder instead). Every variable has a sensible default; a checkout with an empty .env runs.

    VariableDefaultWhat it does
    ANTHROPIC_API_KEYemptyKey for the boardroom’s language-model calls. Empty → mock mode, automatically.
    BABLYTICS_MODELclaude-opus-4-8The Anthropic model every seat uses. Shown read-only in Settings.
    BABLYTICS_HOST127.0.0.1Bind address. Leave it on loopback unless you understand what exposing a single-password app to your network means.
    BABLYTICS_PORT8420Port for the web server.
    BABLYTICS_MOCKempty1 forces mock mode even with a key.
    BABLYTICS_DATA_DIRdata/ in the checkoutMoves the data folder (new in 2.0). The packaged app uses it too.
    QUIVER_API_KEYemptyQuiver Quantitative key for live congressional-trade disclosures (24 h cache). Without it the collector tries the legacy public dumps, which currently return 403, and the Watchdog reports “no signal”.
    SCHWAB_APP_KEY / SCHWAB_APP_SECRETemptyOptional Schwab developer-app credentials. They can instead be entered in the Broker view, where they are stored masked in the database; the database copy wins.
    SCHWAB_CALLBACK_URLhttps://127.0.0.1:8421/schwab/callbackMust match the callback registered on your Schwab app. It never has to serve anything — the OAuth flow is paste-the-redirect.

    STONKS_MODEL, STONKS_HOST, STONKS_PORT and STONKS_MOCK are honoured as fallbacks for the four renamed variables.

    Mock mode#

    No key, no cost, still the whole machine. With no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (or with BABLYTICS_MOCK=1) every session — the morning briefing, the Pre-Open Check, the Midday Check-In, the Evening Court, the horizon reviews, the Pulse’s rationales — runs on deterministic heuristics written in each persona’s spirit instead of language-model calls. The output has exactly the same shape, the UI shows a MOCK MODE pill so you always know which board you are talking to, and the market data is still live. If even the market scan fails (you are offline), the scanner substitutes a synthetic candidate list so the pipeline can still be demonstrated end to end. Mock mode is where every feature in this Guide was first exercised; it is a first-class mode, not a stub.

    Where data goes in a checkout#

    Everything lands in data/ (git-ignored): bablytics.db, cache/, model.joblib, rl/ (the Pulse’s models), members/ (dossiers), boardroom/ (close packets and the owner’s own morning/evening artifacts), schwab_tokens.json if you connect Schwab, universe.json if you refresh the universe. Delete the folder to reset the app; copy it to back it up (quit first, or at least copy the -wal and -shm sidecars with the database). Data & privacy lists what each piece holds.

    The schedule runs inside the process#

    All the timed sessions — 7:00 briefing, 9:15 Pre-Open, 12:30 Midday, the half-hourly Pulse and quarter-hourly Bailiff during the session, 16:45 outcomes, 19:00 Evening Court, the weekend horizons — are APScheduler cron jobs inside the server process, in America/New_York time. They fire only while the server is running and the machine is awake; a job missed during sleep is skipped, not replayed. Every session has a Run now button in the UI for exactly that case. If you want the rhythm unattended, run the server on a machine that stays on (a Mac mini, a small VPS bound to loopback behind SSH, a home server) — see How a day runs for what each job does and Settings for which times are editable.

    The Guide at /about/#

    This documentation lives in site/ and is built by a stdlib-only script:

    python3 site/build.py            # writes site/index.html, site/<page>.html, search-index.json
python3 site/build.py --check    # exit 1 on dangling links, missing screenshots, duplicate ids
python3 site/build.py --single   # also writes site/bablytics-guide.html, one shareable file

    When site/index.html exists, the server mounts the folder at /about/ — no sign-in required, it is documentation — and the dashboard’s nav shows a Guide link. The packaged apps carry the built site inside the bundle, which is why the Guide is readable offline from the desktop app. Preview the static folder on its own with python3 -m http.server 8080 from inside site/.

    The desktop window from source#

    ./.venv/bin/pip install -r requirements-desktop.txt   # pywebview, pyinstaller, pillow
./.venv/bin/python -m bablytics.desktop               # native window on the local server
BABLYTICS_BROWSER=1 ./.venv/bin/python -m bablytics.desktop     # serve + open your browser
BABLYTICS_NO_WINDOW=1 ./.venv/bin/python -m bablytics.desktop   # headless; prints BABLYTICS READY <url>

    bablytics.desktop is what the packaged apps run: it starts the server in a thread, waits for /api/auth/status to answer, then opens a pywebview window (Cocoa on macOS, Edge WebView2 on Windows, GTK WebKit or Qt on Linux). If the window toolkit is missing it falls back to your browser and keeps serving.

    Building the apps yourself#

    PyInstaller cannot cross-compile, so each platform builds its own: packaging/build_desktop.sh on macOS (→ dist/Bablytics.app, Bablytics-mac-<arch>.zip and .dmg), packaging/build_windows.ps1 on Windows (→ the zip and, if Inno Setup 6 is present, the setup.exe), packaging/build_linux.sh on Linux (→ the tarball). Each script ends by running packaging/smoke_test.py against what it built, with its own port and a temporary data folder. packaging/README.md has the per-OS notes and signing caveats; packaging/RELEASING.md describes cutting a release and how .github/workflows/desktop-builds.yml does the same on GitHub’s runners. The artifact names are fixed and unversioned — the ones on the download page.

    Command-line tools worth knowing#

    python -m bablytics.universe refresh
    Re-fetches the S&P 500 constituent list from Wikipedia and writes data/universe.json, which overrides the snapshot baked into the code (503 tickers as of 2026-08-18). This is the only time the app contacts Wikipedia.
    python -m bablytics.boardroom.dossier
    Regenerates every member’s markdown dossier under data/members/ from the database (the Evening Court does this automatically).
    python -m bablytics.bailiff.triggers
    Runs the Bailiff’s hand-labelled corpus and prints its parsing precision/recall — the measured honesty of the invalidation parser.
    python -m bablytics.boardroom.evening_collect
    Reprices today’s book at the close into data/boardroom/<date>/close_packet.json, for the court to read.
    node check_studies.js
    Golden-value checks for the thirty chart studies in web/terminal.js.

    Keeping changes honest#

    Before you send anything: ./.venv/bin/python -m py_compile on every touched module (3.9!), node --check web/app.js for the front end, python3 site/build.py --check if you touched the Guide, and packaging/smoke_test.py "./.venv/bin/python -m bablytics.desktop" for the desktop path. Keep the disclaimer strip on every view, keep the research-tool framing — nothing in the code trades for anyone — and never touch the users or sessions tables in a migration.
